title: What to see in the Riviera Maya: 7 beaches, towns and Maya sites
description: Seven Riviera Maya places, from Puerto Morelos and Playa del Carmen to Akumal, Tulum and Cobá, with beach access, admission and regional planning.
keyword: what to see in the Riviera Maya
relatedQueries: things to do in Riviera Maya
what to see in the Riviera Maya itinerary
intro: To choose what to see in the Riviera Maya, this guide develops seven different places: Puerto Morelos, Playa del Carmen, Xpu-Há, Akumal, Puerto Aventuras, Tulum archaeological site and Cobá. It combines towns, beaches, a marina and Maya heritage, including an inland outing.

These are not seven stops to rush through in one day. Choose the group that suits your base and the kind of visit you want to purchase or reserve. Every place has an individual archive photograph, and changing details use official sources consulted on 5 November 2026.

sections.heading: 1. Puerto Morelos: a coastal town and leaning lighthouse
paragraphs: Puerto Morelos introduces the Riviera Maya at the scale of a seaside town. Its old leaning lighthouse marks the waterfront, while the destination is associated with the reef and boat outings. For a straightforward visit, separate walking around the coastal centre from any booked activity on the water. They require different arrangements.

The Mexican Caribbean tourism office describes the town and its inland connections. Proximity should not be translated into a guaranteed journey time from an airport or hotel. If booking an outing, check the dock, included equipment, weather conditions and return arrangements. The lighthouse photograph is an archive image identifying the place without promising an empty beach, particular sea conditions or available excursions. Choose a stop that works even if the water-based part of your plan changes.

sections.heading: 2. Playa del Carmen: an urban base beside the Caribbean
paragraphs: Playa del Carmen combines an urban centre of shops and restaurants with the coast. Fifth Avenue helps orient a first walk, but the destination extends beyond one shopping street. It can work as a base for alternating urban services with regional outings, provided you check the accommodation’s position and connections for your intended visits.

Decide whether the stop is a walk, meal or the start of a transfer. A terminal, pier and hotel sharing the name Playa del Carmen are not necessarily adjacent. The aerial photograph illustrates the relationship between town and beach, rather than a particular entrance or current swimming conditions. Shopping and beach services are optional. Compare their inclusions instead of assuming they form part of access to the public waterfront.

sections.heading: 3. Xpu-Há: a beach with access choices
paragraphs: Xpu-Há lies south of Playa del Carmen and appears in the Mexican Caribbean’s official beach guide as an option with a more rustic setting. Its appeal is time beside the coast rather than adding another complicated excursion. The sand and water in the documentary photograph belong to the moment it was taken. Sargassum, waves and visibility may differ when you arrive.

The tourism source mentions beach clubs with admission charges and spending conditions. Check the particular entrance, amount and whether any credit applies to purchases. We do not turn some businesses’ practices into a universal rule. Check parking or your pickup point too. A beach stop works better when you know where to enter and how to leave, rather than getting off transport at an unspecified highway location.

sections.heading: 4. Akumal: the bay and responsible wildlife observation
paragraphs: Akumal is known for its bay and sea turtles, but visiting should not be treated as a guaranteed encounter or an invitation to approach animals. The official beach guide highlights restrictions on touching and feeding. Choose the beach and any activity with respect for permitted areas, local instructions and sea conditions.

For a guided experience, verify the operator, route, equipment, participation conditions and cost before booking. An older photograph of people in the water is not proof of unrestricted present-day access to every sector. You can appreciate the scenery without booking a wildlife activity. If environmental conditions cancel an outing, entering independently is not an appropriate substitute. The archive image shows the bay and boats rather than promising visible turtles. Give conservation instructions priority over obtaining a photograph.

sections.heading: 5. Puerto Aventuras: a marina within a residential community
paragraphs: Puerto Aventuras offers a different setting: boats, a marina and a residential-tourism community. Its operator describes nautical services, dining and other activities. Choose it to explore that environment or use a particular service without confusing it with a public square offering unrestricted admission to every facility in the complex.

Before travelling, check visitor conditions and the entrance for your intended business or activity. A restaurant booking, boat outing and sports-facility visit need not share inclusions. The photograph shows a boat moored in the marina. It does not imply that the same vessel currently offers a bookable excursion. Animal-interaction experiences are not recommended here as an automatic addition to a harbour walk. Make the marina itself or a specifically chosen service the reason for your visit.

sections.heading: 6. Tulum archaeological site: ruins and separate fees
paragraphs: Tulum’s archaeological site occupies a walled coastal setting, distinct from the destination’s town centre and hotels. INAH describes Eastern Coast-style architecture, and El Castillo identifies the site in the photograph. Approach it as an archaeological visit, allowing time to interpret structures and landscape without assuming a beach ticket or another park product covers everything.

The listing consulted on 5 November 2026 published hours of 08:00–17:00, with last admission at 15:30. It listed INAH admission at MXN 105 for national visitors or MXN 210 for foreign visitors, plus separate GAFSACOMM and CONANP fees with their own categories. We do not present INAH admission as the total cost. Check eligibility, exemptions and your product’s inclusions, identify the exact approach and leave time to reach the entrance.

sections.heading: 7. Cobá: a distinct inland outing
paragraphs: Cobá is inland rather than another beach along the corridor. INAH highlights its raised roads, or sacbe’ob, and monuments such as Nohoch Mul within a setting of vegetation and lagoons. Visit to understand how a Maya city was organised and connected with other settlements rather than treating it solely as a pyramid photograph.

The official listing consulted indicated daily opening from 08:00 to 17:00, last admission at 16:00 and regular entry of MXN 105 for national visitors or MXN 210 for foreign visitors. Separate this from transport and optional site services. Older photographs do not establish permission to climb structures: follow the currently authorised routes. Plan outward and return travel with a buffer. The road journey makes Cobá unsuitable as a few spare minutes added after a beach stop.

sections.heading: A long region: choose a base before booking excursions
paragraphs: The Riviera Maya is a region rather than one town. Its official tourism source links Puerto Morelos, Playa del Carmen and Tulum, with Highway 307 and bus or train connections requiring an onward final leg. A station bearing the destination’s name is not the entrance to your hotel or monument. Check which airport suits your chosen base as well.

Budget separately for accommodation, transfers, archaeological admission, beach access or purchases and activities. Quoted hours were consulted on 5 November 2026. A booked excursion still needs its current inclusions checked. We do not promise calm seas, turtles, no sargassum or constant driving times. Keep a cultural alternative when water activities are unsuitable.

itinerary: Northern group: choose Puerto Morelos or Playa del Carmen as the main walk according to accommodation and connections. Exploring one centre carefully is more useful than turning both into photographs from a vehicle window.
Beach and marina group: compare Xpu-Há, Akumal and Puerto Aventuras by the specific experience and entrance. They are not interchangeable activities and do not require visiting all three together.

Archaeological group: give Tulum time of its own and arrange a separate inland outing for Cobá when the journey makes sense. Their last admission times differ. A coastal base does not remove road travel or the final approach to each entrance.

faq.question: Can you visit all seven places in one day?
faq.answer: We do not recommend it. Distances, access arrangements and activities make choosing a nearby group and spreading the remainder across other outings more useful.

faq.question: Is the INAH ticket Tulum’s complete cost?
faq.answer: The consulted listing includes separate GAFSACOMM and CONANP fees. Verify your category, exemptions and reservation inclusions before adding or comparing amounts.

faq.question: Is swimming with turtles guaranteed in Akumal?
faq.answer: No. Wildlife and environmental conditions cannot be guaranteed. Respect areas and instructions and check authorised services for your date.

faq.question: Is Cobá beside Tulum’s beach?
faq.answer: It is a separate inland outing with its own transfer. Do not treat it as an immediate extra stop along the hotel strip.

conclusion: Choose for location and experience rather than the number of excursions purchased. Allowing time for each place and checking access, conditions and return travel makes the Riviera Maya easier to explore.
